3_cross_quantity_liquid_T_dependence.finding: S_ex(2200) - S_ex(1900) is +0.32 to +0.73 J/mol-atom/K (0.9-2.3 sd), i.e. Cp_ex = +2.2 to +5.0 J/mol-atom/K, but the same runs give H_mix(2200) - H_mix(1900) of -4.8, -1.1, -0.3 kJ/mol-atom (x_Ni 0.25, 0.5, 0.75), i.e. Cp_ex of -16, -4, -1 J/mol-atom/K. The two estimates of Cp_ex have opposite signs (dH - T dS = -6.5, -2.2, -0.8 sd; the Cr-rich state fails clearly), so the 1900-2200 K difference is not a thermodynamically consistent temperature dependence of the excess Gibbs energy. The Cr-rich 1900 K reference is an undercooled liquid that crystallised after 82 ps (analysed over 80 ps). Read as a sampling/reference effect, not as evidence for a T^2 or T ln T term; no term added. All six S_ex values stay in the fit at their u (flag).
3_cross_quantity_liquid_T_dependence.decision: L0, L1 of the liquid kept a + bT; reported, no extra term
